one_liner: Embedded C++20 query engine over memory-mapped OpenStreetMap GOL files; claims 50x faster queries than an SQL database.
what_it_does: libgeodesk is the C++ port of GeoDesk, an in-process, serverless database for OpenStreetMap data stored in its own Geo-Object Library (.gol) format. You open a GOL as a Features collection, filter it with a CSS-like tag query language (e.g. "na[amenity=pub]"), chain spatial filters (within, containing, maxMetersFromLonLat) and iterate lightweight Feature objects, with direct access to tags, way nodes, relation members and parent relations. It replaces a PostGIS/osm2pgsql-style import plus SQL queries, not a geometry library: geometric operations beyond length/area need the optional GEOS integration. GOL files are built from .osm.pbf with the separate Java-based gol tool or assembled from downloadable tiles.
how_it_is_fast: The GOL file is memory-mapped (clarisma::FreeStore over MemoryMapping) and queried in place, with no row decoding or ORM layer. Data is partitioned into a tile pyramid walked depth-first against the query box (TileIndexWalker), and each tile holds separate spatial indexes for nodes, ways, areas and relations, each an R-tree whose branches carry a bitmask of indexed tag keys so branches lacking the queried keys are skipped before any bounding-box test. Tag queries are compiled into matchers, strings are interned in a global string table, and tiles are scanned in parallel by a thread-pool of TileQueryTask workers.
when_to_use: Repeated tag-plus-area queries over OSM extracts (country or planet) from a C++ program, where running and importing into PostGIS is the alternative.
Desktop or batch tools that need OSM relation semantics (route members, multipolygon areas, parent relations) without an SQL schema.
Low-ops deployments: a single read-mostly file, no database server, any 64-bit Windows, Linux or macOS machine.
Region-scoped workflows that can download pre-made tiles instead of processing a full planet PBF.
when_not_to_use: Non-OSM geometry: it indexes only GOL-encoded OSM features, not your own polygons or point clouds; use TG, GEOS or an R-tree library for those.

When you need the claimed speedup proven: the README ratios (50x queries, 20x import, under one tenth of SQL storage) have no methodology, hardware, dataset or named database, and the repo's only benchmark times GeoDesk alone against hard-coded local Windows paths.
Heavy transactional writes or arbitrary SQL joins and aggregates; the engine is a read-mostly query API.
Toolchains without solid C++20 support or projects that cannot accept LGPL-3.0 linking terms; an open issue (#34) lists GCC 14.3 / Clang 19 install and link failures on Linux.
Regional extracts where area relations may be incomplete: open bug #43 says such relations can still match as areas (false positives).

integration.dependencies: gtl (greg7mdp, fetched by CMake); optional GEOS and GDAL/OGR; Catch2 for tests; Java 16+ for the separate gol build tool
integration.thread_safety: Single-threaded query access by default; the CMake option GEODESK_MULTITHREADED enables sharing one GOL across threads (atomic refcounts). Each query internally fans tile scans out to a thread pool.

gotchas: Builds a static library by default (BUILD_SHARED_LIBS forced OFF in CMakeLists.txt); shared builds need GEODESK_SHARED handling.
RelWithDebInfo builds strip NDEBUG (-U NDEBUG), so assertions stay on; benchmark with Release.
Without the GOL tool (Java) you cannot create GOL files from .osm.pbf; an open issue (#36) asks for in-process conversion.
Open todo issues note missing guards for truncated files (#40) and extremely large GOQL queries (#42), and a reported segfault when a .gol file is not found (#34).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it when the data is OpenStreetMap and the alternative is an osm2pgsql/PostGIS import; TG or GeoToolbox are better when you need fast predicates or indexes over your own geometries rather than an OSM feature store.
verified_claims_summary: Only first-party README slogans exist: queries 'typically 50 times faster than SQL', GOL build '20 times faster than an import into an SQL database', and GOL files 20% to 50% larger than the source PBF and under a tenth of SQL storage, with no hardware, compiler, dataset or named database. The repo's Catch2 benchmark times 1,000 containing() queries on Western European admin areas and a count of all US buildings, GeoDesk only, with no SQL baseline.
status_note: Actively developed by one main author (last commit 2026-09-28, 186 commits, 20 stars) with Java and Python siblings; LGPL-3.0-only, so check the license's relinking terms before shipping the default static build inside a closed-source product.
